clue.text: Tree's stock lacking core

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter synonym is taken away, as the core of something is its centre

parts.note: a stock answer or phrase is a common, widely used one, so stock means popular

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk or rootstock that has rotted away at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking core' removes the central U from POPULAR. 'Stock' looks like a tree's trunk or rootstock, but here it means standard or popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall, fast-growing deciduous tree of the willow family, often planted in rows.

clue.text: Troop is told to carry weapon

indicators.note: the words of the phrase carry the answer within them, spanning the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Soldiers are ordered to bear arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' signals that the letters are held inside 'trooP IS TOLd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a small firearm, one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Hound is, by itself, endearing

parts.note: the Latin phrase per se means by itself or intrinsically
something endearing is cute or sweet

explanation.surface: A dog that is lovable just as it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a dog, but it is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to pursue and harass them relentlessly, a synonym.

clue.text: Fused dead part without resistance is changed

indicators.note: fused letters are melted together and recast, so the fodder is reworked into a new order

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An electrical fault: a blown, dead component altered once its resistor is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without resistance' takes R out of the letters of DEAD PART; 'Fused' then rearranges what is left, DEADPAT, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adapted has been modified or altered to suit new conditions, a synonym.

clue.text: Solitary ego torn apart about love

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

indicators.note: the critical word goes round the letter for love

parts.note: to be torn apart by critics is to be slated, harshly criticised
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lonely self, wrecked by heartbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside SLATED, the British word for savagely criticised, giving SOLATED after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary and alone both describe something set apart from others, a synonym.

clue.text: Dodge seeing raincoat's lifted

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat; with the 's it gives MACS

explanation.surface: A trick involving a stolen raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' looks like stolen, but in a down clue it turns MAC'S upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a swindle or con trick, a synonym.

clue.text: Match — one made in Heaven that fell?

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match struck to make fire

definitions.text: one made in Heaven that fell?
definitions.meaning: the angel created in Heaven who rebelled and was cast down, becoming Satan

explanation.surface: A marriage made in heaven that fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to early strike-anywhere matches, and is also the fallen angel of Christian tradition.

clue.text: Note following article's subject

indicators.note: the note comes after the article in the answer

parts.note: the definite article is the word the
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A memo about the subject of a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject matter of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Sticky end of girl's flower

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana; with the 's it gives DIS
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: The glutinous tip of a girl's flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky end' is an idiom for a calamitous fate, not a gummy tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a sticky end is to meet with catastrophe, so the idiom means a calamity.

clue.text: Corn reportedly in a row

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for corn is spoken

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Corn planted in a straight row.
explanation.definitionFit: Serial things happen in sequence, one after another, like items placed in a row.

clue.text: Organ groove is endless after pot

indicators.note: the trimmed groove comes after the pot in the answer

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym for groove is dropped

parts.note: a crease is a groove or fold line

explanation.surface: An organ grinder, or a potter's endless groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last E of CREASE to give CREAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland behind the stomach producing insulin and digestive enzymes, an internal organ.

clue.text: Extra work noticeable by current compiler

parts.note: overt means open and plainly noticeable
I is the symbol for electric current
the crossword compiler refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter working conspicuously late hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossword's compiler is the setter, who often stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is work done beyond normal hours, extra labour.

clue.text: Animal, hurt cat is raised

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An injured cat is lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' reverses TOM to MOT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing rodent of mountainous regions, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Wants to sell top Queen single initially

parts.note: to top is slang for to kill, as is to off
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word single is taken

explanation.surface: Pop chart talk: a leading Queen single on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like chart-topping but is slang for kill, OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer goods is to put them up and show you want to sell them.

clue.text: Location occupied by heart of royalty?

definitions.text: Location occupied by heart of royalty?

indicators.note: the place is filled by the central letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: a place is a location

indicators.note: only the central letter of the seven-letter word royalty is taken

explanation.surface: A building where the very core of the monarchy lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of royalty' is the A at the centre of ROYALTY, put inside PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal residence is a place occupied by kings and queens, the core of the monarchy.

clue.text: Apparatus for landing gear in a cruder alternative

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters means they are reordered

explanation.surface: A plane's landing gear swapped for a rougher version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' looks part of the definition but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheels and struts under an aircraft, used for taking off and landing.

clue.text: Hires out a dodgy permit

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shady hire company handing out a suspect licence.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to give official permission for something, a synonym of permit as a verb.

clue.text: Officer material, ace joining Nato oddly

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word Nato are taken

explanation.surface: Good officer material, an ace pilot, joins the military alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of NATO, N and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer in the army or a police rank, an example of an officer.

clue.text: One's attractive to men with lager etc drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests being in a disordered state, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man who becomes attractive to men after lager has been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's attractive' looks like a person's charm, but describes a device that attracts iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil-wound magnet that attracts metal when current flows, so it is something attractive.

clue.text: Blithe or emotionless accepting proposition

indicators.note: the phrase accepts the answer inside it, across its word boundaries

explanation.surface: A cheerful or cold person accepting a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the letters inside 'bliTHE OR EMotionless'.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proposition is a statement to be proved, a synonym.

clue.text: More crackers in barrel overturned on floor

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed barrel sits on top of the floor
the word for the barrel is turned over, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
a tier is a level or floor

explanation.surface: Christmas crackers stored in a barrel tipped on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses TUN to NUT. 'Crackers' is British slang for mad, not party novelties.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for mad, so more crackers is madder, a comparative synonym.

clue.text: Boat crew supporting wide load

indicators.note: in a down entry the crew sits beneath, supporting the letter above

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide ball
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing crew carrying a wide, heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy load or burden that must be carried.

clue.text: Government's leader expressed hesitation getting stuck

indicators.note: the leader of the word Government is its first letter

parts.note: to umm is to say um, hesitating

explanation.surface: The prime minister hesitated and got stuck for words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glued or pasted has been fixed in place, so the word means stuck.

clue.text: Little time to go round the Italian city

indicators.note: the time unit goes round the article, enclosing it

parts.note: min is the short form of minute, a little time
la is the Italian feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A quick tour round an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian city' looks like the definition, but 'the Italian' gives LA, leaving 'city' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern Italian fashion capital is an example of a city.

clue.text: Former wife in diet ends increased sugar

indicators.note: the former wife goes inside those first and last letters
the first and last letters of the word diet are taken

parts.note: an ex is a former wife or partner
rose is a past tense of rise, increased

explanation.surface: An ex-wife whose sugar intake rose despite a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes D and T from DIET; EX goes inside them to give DEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose, a simple sugar, is also called by this name: an example of sugar.

clue.text: Soon to be nameless, shortly

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for soon or in a little while
the shortened form of anonymous, without a known name

explanation.surface: Someone about to lose their name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means soon in old English and is the usual abbreviation used for an unknown author.

clue.text: Inviting everyone round to catch United

indicators.note: the pair of words catch the letter between them

parts.note: all means everyone
a ring is a circle, something round
U is a standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Everyone is invited to come round and see United play.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring is tempting and enticing, much like inviting in the sense of attractive.

clue.text: Recording of affair entrapping one

indicators.note: the affair surrounds and traps the numeral

parts.note: a fling is a short romantic affair
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A recording of an illicit affair trapping someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Filing is the recording and storing of documents in an ordered system.

clue.text: Housing people imprisoned by conviction

indicators.note: the people are locked inside the belief word

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or firmly held conviction
men are people

explanation.surface: Prison housing for people with criminal convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests a court verdict but here means a belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building of rented flats, a form of housing.

clue.text: Father meddles with Time

parts.note: to pry is to meddle nosily, so meddles is pries

explanation.surface: Old Father Time interfering in human affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Time' reads as one figure, but 'Father' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic and Anglican clergy are addressed as Father, so a priest is one example.
